svg.aria-label: Four Lewis structures that students drew, each in its own box. (a) Methanol, CH3OH, as drawn: carbon bonded to three H and to O, and the O bonded to one H with three lone pairs. Corrected: the O has two lone pairs. Error: too many electrons; the drawing uses 16 electrons but methanol has 14. (b) Formaldehyde, H2C=O: carbon bonded to two H and double-bonded to O, which has two lone pairs. This one is correct: 12 electrons, carbon has four bonds, oxygen has two bonds and two lone pairs. (c) Ethanethiol, CH3CH2SH, as drawn: the sulfur has two bonds and only one lone pair. Corrected: the sulfur has two lone pairs. Error: octet not satisfied; S has only 6 electrons. (d) Methylamine, as drawn: the nitrogen is bonded to the carbon and to three H, with no lone pair. Corrected: CH3NH2, nitrogen bonded to carbon and two H with one lone pair. Error: four bonds and no lone pair is the pattern of a positive nitrogen, as in CH3NH3+.

g.text: Too many electrons: O has 3 lone pairs (16 e−; needs 14)
Correct: 12 e−, C has 4 bonds, O has 2 bonds + 2 lone pairs
Octet not satisfied: S with one lone pair has only 6 e−
Wrong bond count: 4 bonds, no lone pair is N+ (CH3NH3+)
